title: Where my Leonard Bernstein heads at???

commenti.body: Oh good, I wasn't onboard with all of this stuff you were talking about until the end of your post. Yes, when I see Cooper in a film or his face at any time, I get a visceral gagging sensation like a snake got into my house or a spider into my bed-- my immediate instinct is to stamp it out.
Why? I don't know. It's an instrinctual response. That's like asking someone to explain why they are grossed out by certain sensations.

I’m conflicted. I knew Sheri Greenawald and I find it creepy that he not only had an affair with her, but wrote a role for her in A Quiet Place. I’ve never heard a nice story about him. He was a sex pest, but also arrogant and rude. People who are rude to service workers are a red flag. He did a great Shostakovich 5. But in the industry he’s remembered as a sex fiend and a smug jerk.
Unsure why you're getting downvoted. This is me with Owen Wilson, Matt Damon and one or two others (but especially Owen Wilson). It's not explainable.
Yeah it's not a rational thing. It's an honest reaction I have and some people have to certain actors and certain people. I believe there could be something in the evolutionary biology history of it.

> But in the industry he’s remembered as a sex fiend and a smug jerk.

....and a genius, surely?

> “Oscar Bait”. Aside from his creative accomplishments,

Bernstein's accomplishments are not the movie's accomplishments and vice versa.  The movie may or may not be Oscar bait, but the man the movie is about is not.

I don't see the purpose of the movie.  It can only aspire toward gossip.

People who enjoy Bernstein's compositions and performances as conductor and his programs (such as the Young People's concerts and the Norton Lectures) and his books such as The Joy of Music and who benefitted from his mentoring and so on and so on and so on have no need of what little of all of that this movie might superficially present.

The funniest aspect of the nose business is: who cares?  A man is not a nose (other than perhaps in Gogol), and yet this is what the movie will offer.  I'll stick with the scores, the performances, the books, and so on.

I think people that dismiss the work of artists and musicians based on gossip are the worst kind of person. They are philistines that are far worse that the people they come out against. They use small issues as a way to dismiss a person's entire body of work because they're too intellectually lazy to actually reckon with the work itself. These people should be put on an island where they will only be exposed to Disney films and leave the rest of humanity alone.

>in the industry he’s remembered as a sex fiend and a smug jerk

this is maybe line items number 4 or 5 after little things like “greatest american conductor”, “benefactor of the arts”, “architect of youth music programs”, etc etc
This is why I hate the internet.
